runtime_boundary: Represents the mlc-ai/web-llm package: its TypeScript API, prebuilt-model registry, and the browser-side MLCEngine that runs entirely inside a web page through WebGPU and WebAssembly, with no local server process. It is published, versioned, and licensed separately from mlc-ai/mlc-llm, the sibling record covering the Python compiler, CLI, and REST server; both consume the same compiled MLC model format, but a genuinely new model architecture still depends on mlc-llm's Python compilation pipeline to produce the WASM model library this package loads. WebLLM Chat (chat.webllm.ai) and the community web-llm-chat project are demonstration and third-party chat applications built on this engine, not part of the reviewed package, so it stays on the runtime side of the ADR 015 test.
model_management: Prebuilt models are referenced by ID against webllm.prebuiltAppConfig.model_list (for example Llama-3-8B-Instruct-q4f32_1-MLC), which points at MLC-quantized weights hosted on the Hugging Face Hub and a matching WebGPU-targeted WASM model library; the browser fetches and reuses both, though official docs do not specify the underlying cache API or eviction behavior. A new quantized variant of an already-supported architecture can be registered as a custom ModelRecord pointing at Hub-hosted weights without local compilation; a genuinely new architecture still requires running mlc_llm compile with the separate Python package to produce a new WASM model library before it can be registered the same way. There is no documented command to list, pin, or remove cached model artifacts from within the library itself.
hardware_requirements: The only documented requirement is a WebGPU-capable browser; the project points users at a recent Chrome release and an external WebGPU support-check tool. No CPU-only fallback, minimum VRAM, or non-Chrome compatibility matrix is stated in official sources, so behavior on other WebGPU-shipping browsers is unconfirmed.
operational_controls: The JavaScript API exposes chat-completion parameters including temperature, JSON-mode and grammar-constrained structured generation, and streaming, plus explicit engine construction options for Web Worker and Service Worker offload and progress callbacks during model loading. There is no documented authentication, metrics endpoint, health endpoint, or request-level tracing; the runtime executes inside the host page's own security context and origin.
strengths: Runs a full OpenAI-compatible chat-completion API, including streaming and JSON-mode structured generation, entirely client-side with no inference server to operate or secure.
First-class Web Worker, Service Worker, and Chrome-extension integration patterns let a host application offload inference off the main thread without a separate runtime process.
Reuses MLC LLM's compiled model libraries and Hugging Face-hosted quantized weights, so architectures already supported by the desktop engine reach the browser without a parallel compilation effort.
tradeoffs: Execution is documented against a single accelerator path, WebGPU in Chrome, with no stated CPU fallback or cross-browser compatibility matrix from official sources.
Serving is inherently single-stream, one browser tab per user, with no batching, request queuing, or multi-user concurrency of any kind.
A genuinely new model architecture still depends on mlc-llm's separate Python compiler to produce a WASM model library, so the package cannot originate full compilation support on its own.
No authentication, metrics endpoint, health endpoint, or request tracing is documented; observability is whatever the host web application builds around the library.
license_note: The repository publishes its own verbatim Apache-2.0 license file, separate from and identical in terms to mlc-ai/mlc-llm's license file; no additional NOTICE or component-specific terms were found.
